cross_reactivity.provenance: Transcribed unchanged from DREAM; awaits clinical sign-off.

items.info: Quaternary ammonium compounds are thought to be responsible for most reactions. Cross-reactivity between agents is common due to structural similarities.
items.alternatives: Consider non-depolarising agents with different structures. Cisatracurium may have lower immunogenicity.

items.info: Cross-reactivity with cephalosporins depends on side chain similarity. First-generation cephalosporins have higher cross-reactivity (~2%).
items.alternatives: Cephalosporins with dissimilar side chains, carbapenems (low cross-reactivity), or non-beta-lactams.

items.info: Cross-reactivity is more related to R1 side chain similarity than the beta-lactam ring. Later generations have different side chains.
items.alternatives: Cephalosporins with different side chains, carbapenems, aztreonam (minimal cross-reactivity).

items.info: True allergy is rare (<1%). Most reactions are vasovagal or due to adrenaline. Amide types rarely cross-react with each other.
items.alternatives: Different amide local anaesthetic, or ester type if amide allergy confirmed.

items.info: Can cause direct mast cell degranulation (non-IgE mediated). Morphine and codeine are most histamine-releasing.
items.alternatives: Fentanyl or remifentanil (less histamine release), or non-opioid analgesia.

items.info: Propofol reactions may be to the lipid emulsion or specific to propofol. Egg/soya allergy is not a contraindication.
